generatedProse.concept-context: In practice, a good search begins before you type anything. Whatever your subject, you decide what claim you need to support and what kind of source would support it, then set a date range to match. A question about settled knowledge points you towards overviews and reference works, while a live debate points you towards recent studies. Deciding this first is how you avoid results that were never going to fit the question.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Consider two students preparing sources for the same assignment, and both begin to search.

Student A opens the library search tool and types the whole assignment title straight in. Thousands of results come back, so Student A skims the first page and takes whatever looks relevant. There was no objective and no plan, so the search returned everything and nothing.

Student B stops to plan first. Student B decides what the question really needs, whether recent studies or established overviews, and sets a sensible date range. Only then does the search begin, and the first page of results is already close to usable.

Both ran a search. Student B did the thinking before the search, and the plan did most of the work.
generatedProse.summary: Planning a search means deciding, before you type, what claim you need to support and what kind of source will support it. A current debate needs recent work; settled knowledge may rest on overviews and reference sources. You can now set an objective and choose a source type and date range for a search of your own. The next lesson builds the keywords that drive it.

check.body: In the worked example, what did Student B do before starting to search?

items.text: Set a clear objective and chose the source type and date range to fit it.
Typed the whole assignment title straight into the search box.
Skimmed the first page of results and took what looked relevant.
Read every result the search returned before choosing.

feedback.correct: That's right. Student B planned the search: a clear objective, then a matching source type and date range.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Student B decided before the search, not during it.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Before searching, Student B set an objective and chose a source type and date range. Typing the title or skimming results is the unplanned approach Student A took.
